title: The Gatekeeper of Cairo and the Cunning She-Thief
summary: At the fortified Bab al-Futuh gate of Cairo stood an old gatekeeper named Uncle Mansur, famous for never letting an unauthorized traveler...
keywords: the gatekeeper of cairo and the cunning she-thief
full_text:
At the fortified Bab al-Futuh gate of Cairo stood an old gatekeeper named Uncle Mansur, famous for never letting an unauthorized traveler or smuggler pass through his portal. He boasted: 'No fly can enter Cairo without my seal!'

One morning, an intelligent young woman named Layla, whose father had been unjustly imprisoned on false charges of tax evasion, resolved to reach the Grand Vizier's diwan inside the citadel. The guards at the gates had been ordered by a corrupt prefect to turn away any petitioners from her village.

Layla approached the gate carrying a large, heavy wicker basket covered with cabbage leaves.
Uncle Mansur barred her way with his spear: 'Halt, girl! What is in the basket?'
Layla replied innocently: 'Only cabbages for the soup kitchens, master.'
Mansur, proud of his thoroughness, thrust his spear into the basket—and out hopped a frightened live hare, which darted between his legs and raced into the busy street!

Mansur and his three guards abandoned their posts, shouting and chasing the hare across the marketplace.
While the guards were scrambling after the animal, Layla calmly walked through the open gate, carrying her second basket containing the legal petitions and accounts proving her father's innocence!

She reached the Grand Vizier, presented the audited books, and secured her father's immediate release.

Returning to the Bab al-Futuh gate that evening, she found Uncle Mansur still breathless, holding the captured hare.
She bowed politely:
'Here are five silver dirhams for thy trouble, Uncle Mansur. The hare was quick, but truth is swifter.'

Uncle Mansur stared, realized how cleanly he had been outmaneuvered, and laughed heartily:
'By Allah, maiden! Thy wit is sharper than my spear. Henceforth, I will inspect what matters to human justice, rather than chasing hares!'
The old gatekeeper became Layla's lifelong friend and defender, learning that wisdom surpasses stubborn brute force.
moral: True security requires vigilant observation and compassion, not mere reliance on iron bars and gruff commands.
